title: Cybersecurity Framework
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
supports: CSF hub with profiles, quick-start guides and informative references; 'Celebrating Two Years of CSF 2.0' on 24 February 2026; final CSF 2.0 Informative References Quick-Start Guide (SP 1347); no CSF 2.1 announced. Opened with WebFetch.

title: NIST releases version 2.0 of landmark Cybersecurity Framework
supports: Released 26 February 2024; six functions with the new Govern function; scope widened to all organisations from small schools and nonprofits to large firms; quick-start guides for small businesses and others; reference catalogue mapping to more than 50 documents. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Quick-Start Guides (CSF 2.0)
supports: CSF 2.0 quick-start guides including Small Business (SP 1300), Organizational Profiles (SP 1301), Tiers (SP 1302), Enterprise Risk Management (SP 1303) and Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (SP 1305). Opened with WebFetch.

title: SP 800-61 Rev. 3: Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management, a CSF 2.0 Community Profile
supports: Published April 2025; builds incident response into cybersecurity risk management using CSF 2.0; supersedes SP 800-61 Rev. 2 (August 2012). Opened with WebFetch.

title: IR 8286 Rev. 1: Integrating Cybersecurity and Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
supports: Published 18 December 2025, superseding IR 8286 (October 2020); guidance on using risk registers to record cybersecurity risk and roll it up to enterprise risk management; companion IR 8286C Rev. 1 on integrating registers. Opened with WebFetch.

title: SP 800-50 Rev. 1: Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program
supports: Published September 2024; life-cycle approach to awareness, training and education for organisations large and small; goal of behaviour change and a security culture; metrics for improvement; supersedes SP 800-50 (2003) and SP 800-16 (1998). Opened with WebFetch.

title: Small Business Cybersecurity Corner
supports: Free small business guidance by topic (ransomware, phishing, MFA, supply chain, solopreneurs) and the Small Business Cybersecurity Support Programs Finder published 5 October 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Phishing Guidance: Stopping the Attack Cycle at Phase One
supports: Joint guide published 18 October 2023 (PDF updated March 2025) on common phishing techniques, for network defenders, software makers and, in a dedicated section, small and medium-sized businesses. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Secure Our World
supports: Four core steps for everyone (avoid and report phishing, strong passwords, MFA and a password manager, update software); small business resources; Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026 toolkit. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Cyber Hygiene Services
supports: No-cost vulnerability scanning of internet-facing assets and web application scanning for US government bodies and public and private critical infrastructure organisations; started by the organisation's own email request. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Scattered Spider (advisory AA23-320A)
publisher: CISA, FBI and partners including the UK NCSC
supports: Published 16 November 2023, revised 29 July 2025: help desk social engineering to reset passwords or move MFA, impersonating IT staff, SIM swapping, MFA fatigue, voice phishing; mitigations include phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO/WebAuthn or PKI), offline encrypted tested backups and application allowlisting. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Phishing attacks: defending your organisation
supports: Four layers of defence; DMARC, SPF and DKIM; verify payment changes by a second channel; training as one layer; no blame and easy reporting; simulations criticised as a primary defence, check with HR before any sanction, reward reporting. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
supports: Official Stripe MCP server at mcp.stripe.com with OAuth or agent API keys; refunds marked for human confirmation in the Dashboard; from December 2026 the server stops accepting full-access secret keys and restricted keys without the Agent tag (migrate by 30 November 2026); advice to turn on tool approval and beware prompt injection. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Small Business Guide: Response and Recovery
supports: Definition of a cyber incident; for a live attack call 0300 123 2040 (24/7), reports go to the Report Fraud Analysis Service; report significant attacks to the NCSC; free Cyber Action Toolkit for sole traders and small businesses. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Cyber Essentials: overview
supports: Five technical controls; Cyber Essentials Plus adds independent testing; certification through IASME, from £320 plus VAT by size; organisations under £20m turnover certifying the whole organisation get cyber liability insurance with incident response support. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Reporting a scam email
supports: Forward suspicious emails to the NCSC, do not click links, report suspicious websites by form; 454.8k scam URLs removed as of July 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Exercise in a Box
supports: Free online exercises for small and medium organisations: micro and tabletop exercises, 20 exercises across 12 topics including ransomware, phishing, supply chain and passwords. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Incident affecting ASOS customers
supports: Published 6 October 2026: some ASOS customers received an unauthorised push notification; ASOS said names and contact details were accessed and did not believe card data or passwords were affected; customers told to assume they are affected and watch for scam messages. Opened with WebFetch.

title: When cyber attacks happen: helping organisations recover
publisher: UK National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC blog)
supports: Published 28 July 2026: response and recovery in three stages (first hours and days, a recovery programme to minimum viable operations, longer-term rebuild); use an NCSC-assured incident response firm; practise failover, shutdown and restart, and rebuilding from backups. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Cyber security breaches survey 2025/2026
publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (GOV.UK, official statistics)
supports: Published 30 April 2026; fieldwork August to December 2025; 2,112 businesses and 1,085 charities: 43% of businesses and 28% of charities had a breach or attack in 12 months; phishing 38% of businesses; formal incident response plan 25%; risk assessment 30%; board member responsible 31%; Cyber Essentials held by 5%; prompted awareness 17%; any cyber insurance 47%. Opened with WebFetch (two reads).

title: Internet Crime Report 2025
supports: 1,008,597 complaints and $20.877 billion reported losses in 2025; business email compromise losses $3,046,598,558; more than 3,600 ransomware complaints; businesses reported over $30 million in BEC losses involving AI. PDF downloaded via WebFetch and converted to text.

title: Cybersecurity for Small Business
supports: Dated September 2025: basics, NIST CSF functions, email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), vendor security, cyber insurance, phishing, ransomware, business email imposters and tech support scams; reporting routes ReportFraud.ftc.gov and IC3.gov. Opened with WebFetch.

title: FTC Safeguards Rule: What Your Business Needs to Know
supports: Covers non-bank financial institutions such as tax preparers and mortgage brokers; written security programme with a Qualified Individual, written risk assessment, MFA, training, written incident response plan; some provisions do not apply under 5,000 consumers; notify the FTC within 30 days of discovering a notification event affecting 500 or more consumers, in effect since May 2024. Opened with WebFetch.

title: NIS2 Directive: securing network and information systems
supports: Transposition deadline 17 October 2024; 18 sectors; rules apply mainly to medium and large entities; management can be held accountable; targeted amendments proposed 20 January 2026, estimated to ease compliance for 28,700 companies including 6,200 micro and small; page updated 2 July 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Data breaches (SME data protection guide)
supports: Notify the data protection authority within 72 hours of becoming aware unless the breach is unlikely to pose a risk; tell individuals without undue delay if high risk; record every breach; processors notify controllers without undue delay. Opened with WebFetch.

title: FAQ clarifies new SAQ A eligibility criteria for e-commerce merchants
supports: Posted 28 February 2025: from 1 April 2025, merchants that embed a provider's payment page or form must confirm their site is not susceptible to script attacks, using techniques such as requirements 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 or written confirmation from a PCI DSS compliant provider (FAQ 1588); redirect and fully outsourced merchants are outside this criterion. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Protect yourself from card testing
supports: How card testing works; signs (spike in failed payments and 402 errors, small payments with nonsense names); refund fraudulent payments to avoid disputes; CAPTCHA, login before payment, rate limits, Radar rules; keep secret keys safe. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Fraud analysis
supports: Low, medium or high fraud recommendations; indicators on Basic and higher, recommendations on Grow and higher or with Shopify Payments; manual capture to review before taking payment; temporary IP blocklist after many orders or failed payments from one IP. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Card testing
supports: Card testing runs many small payment attempts or saves cards without buying; Shopify Payments has card testing protection at checkout; cancel high-risk orders before fulfilment (a bank can still file a chargeback), manual capture, Shopify Flow, AVS and CVV filters and the Fraud Control app. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Two-step authentication
supports: Authenticator app or security key; SMS cannot be set up as a new method; staff set up their own two-step authentication and owners cannot turn it on for them, except Shopify Plus, which can require a secure sign-in method. Opened with WebFetch.
